The saved-entry shape (the gh-1990 repro, `copilot-IstiN`), the `/provider copilot` connect flow, and all app/fa_ui surfaces are covered — this only narrows the «never a silent answer» surface for an unsaved active-copilot or env-keyed-copilot provider. comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the constructor doc states an invariant the default `fetchReport` does not satisfy**

> "Creates the report; [diagnostic] must be non-null exactly when [info].$1 is empty — an empty answer always names its reason."

The Copilot dialect honors this (every empty answer carries a diagnostic — verified by the AC1/AC2 matrix). But the **default** `ModelListDialect.fetchReport` (and every non-Copilot dialect, which inherit it) answers empty with a **null** diagnostic — the deliberately preserved legacy shape (the dispatch only names the "no dialect handles this endpoint" case, and the new `non-copilot dialects answer a report with no diagnostic` test pins exactly that). So the stated "exactly when" invariant is false for half the dialect table, and a programmatic consumer that trusts the doc (e.g. asserts `diagnostic != null ⇔ isEmpty`, or unconditionally reads `reasonText` on empty) will misread non-Copilot empty answers.

Reword to scope the contract, e.g.: *"Dialects that override [ModelListDialect.fetchReport] with named failure branches (today the Copilot dialect) attach a diagnostic on every empty answer; the default keeps the legacy diagnostic-less shape (null even when empty)."* The same nuance applies to the `[diagnostic]` field doc ("null exactly when models were listed") and `userFacingReason` (which correctly degrades to `note`/null — the code is right, only the doc overpromises). Wording only, the tests pin the real behavior; does not block merge.

```gitignore
# gh-1986 review: dmtools target-workingdir marker — local tool state,

```

So this is the *second* time a WIP auto-save swept it into a PR — the exact recurrence that comment warns about. It is not referenced anywhere in the PR's code, tests, or CHANGELOG; it is pure scope creep, and once merged it becomes tracked junk in `main` that `.gitignore` can no longer hide (tracking overrides ignores) and that every future branch will see as a deletion conflict.

**Fix:** `git rm --cached .dmtools-target-workingdir` (keep the local file on disk) and re-push. After the rebase onto current `main`, the ignore rule will keep it out for good.

Per gh-1990's implementer guidance, the owner's failing provider (`copilot-IstiN`, OAuth `gho_` token, individual tier) most likely hits exactly this branch: individual-tier `/models` responses omit `model_picker_enabled`, so every entry drops with `picker flag absent` and the list stays empty. > "then — evidence permitting — the likely one-line class fix: **tier-aware filter** — treat `model_picker_enabled` ABSENT (key missing) as selectable when the response comes from the individual host / a no-proxy-ep token (absence ≠ explicit false; an explicit `false` still drops)."

For reference, pi-mono (which this criterion mirrors) already solves the same individual-tier shape at the filter level: `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts` (`badlogic/pi-mono`, read during this review) computes `allowPolicyFallback = baseUrl === "https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com"` and falls back to policy-enabled models when the strict picker list empties — same trigger condition, same endpoint scoping.

**Ask:** confirm a follow-up issue exists (or file one) for the tier-aware filter so the owner-validation loop doesn't stall after the diagnostics land. If AC5 evidence already shows a different branch (exchange 403 / HTTP), say so in the PR description — the filter path is currently only exercised by synthetic bodies.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the combined diagnostic fabricates a `stage` outside the documented vocabulary**

When both credential paths fail, `stage: '${a.stage}+${b.stage}'` produces values like `'exchange+models'`. `ModelsFetchDiagnostic.stage` is new public API whose doc pins a closed set — `stageExchange`, `stageModels`, `stageFilter` ("The stage that produced this: the token exchange, the `/models` HTTP call, or the picker filter") — and any programmatic consumer matching on those constants (the same surfaces the PR says render diagnostics) will silently fail to match the combined value.

Options: add a documented `stageDual` constant (or `stages: List<String>`), or keep `stage` as the primary path's stage and let `message` carry the combination (it already does). No current consumer matches on `stage`, so this is polish — but cheap to fix before the type accretes dependents.

As written this says the opposite of what the code two lines below does: `if (picker == null) return 'picker flag absent';` **drops** the entry (and pi's strict `pickerModelIds` filter in `github-copilot.ts` drops them too — `pickerEnabled: item.model_picker_enabled === true`). comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: unbounded response body embedded in user-facing one-line diagnostics**

The 404/non-200 exchange failures embed `Body: ${response.body.trim()}` verbatim into `CopilotAuthException.message` (pre-existing text, `statusCode` added around it here). With gh-1990 that message now propagates through `ModelsFetchDiagnostic.message` into `fetch notes:` (CLI), the connect sheet, and the app's model field — all single-line UI surfaces. A misconfigured base URL pointing at an HTML endpoint (or a verbose gateway error page) can flood them with an arbitrarily long blob, and the body is shown raw with no redaction layer in front of it.

The exchange endpoint is api.github.com so today's bodies are tame JSON errors, but the cheap hardening is worth it while this code is being touched: cap the embedded body (e.g. `final snippet = response.body.trim(); '${snippet.length > 200 ? '${snippet.substring(0, 200)}…' : snippet}'`). Not a leak today — just future-proofing a string that now reaches five surfaces.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_copilotModelsShapeValid` decodes the body a second time**

`_fetchModelsList` calls `_parseCopilotModelsResponse(response.body)` (which `jsonDecode`s the body and already knows whether `data` is a `List`), then on the empty branch calls `_copilotModelsShapeValid(response.body)`, which `jsonDecode`s the same body again just to re-derive the shape the parser already computed. Have the parser return the shape (or a `dataIsList` flag) and drop the second decode — one less JSON pass on every honest-empty answer, and the "empty list vs unexpected shape" distinction stops depending on a re-parse agreeing with the first one. Related: this helper is also one of the two unguarded `jsonDecode` sites (see the BLOCKING thread on `_fetchModelsList`) — folding it into the parser removes the duplicate hazard too.
